newsitem.title: INDONESIA: INDONESIA LATE RUBBER EASES ON CURRENCY FALL.
newsitem.headline: INDONESIA LATE RUBBER EASES ON CURRENCY FALL.

text.p: Indonesian tyre-grade SIR20 rubber prices eased in late trading on Thursday following the government's move to float the rupiah, traders said.
"Our prime concern now is the currency. We've seen prices slightly softening because of a weaker rupiah. I believe prices can drop to as low as 40.00 (U.S. cents/lb)," said one trader.
The rupiah had stabilised at sharply lower levels in late trading on Thursday after the central bank scrapped its band, dealers said.

Bank Indonesia said it will no longer announce its daily intervention and conversion bands with immediate effect. Spot rupiah was ranging between 2,750 and 2,790 in the afternoon, with some players seen cashing out from dollars.
Spot rupiah fell to a low of 2,800 in thin volume before recovering to 2,760/70 at 0810 GMT from an opening of 2,648/58.
Rubber traders said a weaker rupiah had prompted buyers to put pressure on the prices.

"Buyers will be making use of the situation by asking for cheaper rubber. The market was very quiet until late in the afternoon as most people are still in the dark about what's going to happen next with the rupiah," said one trader.
Traders said demand was weak while supply was generally good in most centres.

"Prices are already weak because of the poor demand while traders are taking a wait-and-see position today. If the rupiah is getting weaker, then the level of 40.00 is not impossible," said one trader.
He said the market would be closely monitoring currency movements in the next few days.
Traders said offer prices were quoted at 42.00 for November/December shipment fob Medan, 42.25 fob Palembang, Surabaya and Padang for October shipment and 41.50 fob Padang for September shipmment.
